meta.notes: Israeli statute-of-limitations rules for sexual offenses, simplified for guidance only. Source: מושגים חשובים.docx and עבירות מין + התיישנות.docx in the 2026-07-20 content haul. This tool NEVER gives legal advice — it returns a direction and always routes to a human. To update: edit the questions or rules blocks below, no code changes needed.
meta.legal_disclaimer: This is a guide, not legal advice. Every case has details a checker can't capture. The rules below are simplified from the Israeli Penal Code (sections 345-352, 428, and the general Statute of Limitations Law). For your specific situation, please talk to Magen or to free legal aid.

questions.help: Choose the range that fits. This helps us estimate the time that has passed.

options.label: I'm under 18
options.note: Different rules apply for minors — you'll be routed to a person.

questions.prompt: How old were you when it happened?
questions.help: If it happened more than once, use the earliest age. If you're not sure, choose your best estimate.

options.label: I'd rather not say
options.note: You can still get a direction — we'll route to a person.

questions.prompt: What was your relationship to the person who hurt you?
questions.help: Israeli law is stricter (and more forgiving on time) when the person had power or family closeness over you.

options.label: A family member (parent, sibling, grandparent, uncle/aunt, in-law, step-family, cousin who was 15 or older)
An authority figure (teacher, therapist, doctor, religious figure, boss, coach, madrich/a)
A peer, acquaintance, or someone I didn't know
I'd rather explain in a conversation

questions.help: There is no wrong answer, and nothing you pick binds you in any way. If you're not sure, pick 'I'd rather explain'.

options.label: Penetration or attempted penetration
options.note: In Israeli law this includes rape (אינוס) and unlawful penetration (חדירה אסורה).

options.label: A sexual act with force, threats, or serious aggravating circumstances (but without penetration)
options.note: In Israeli law this is a severe indecent act (מעשה מגונה בנסיבות מחמירות).

options.label: A non-penetrating sexual act (touching, exposure, or coerced acts)
options.note: In Israeli law this is an indecent act (מעשה מגונה).

options.label: Repeated unwanted comments, propositions, or exposure to sexual content
options.note: In Israeli law this is sexual harassment (הטרדה מינית).

options.label: I'd rather explain in a conversation

rules.headline: This is a situation only a person can answer well.
rules.body: Some parts of your answers, or your age right now, mean the rules aren't well captured by a checker. Please talk to us — it's free and confidential, and we'll walk through it with you.

rules.headline: The window is likely still open for you.
rules.body: When the incident happened before you were 18, and the person had family closeness or authority, the statute of limitations clock typically doesn't begin ticking until you become an adult, and it can run well into your 40s. In some cases it extends to age 49. This is one of the most protective corners of the law for exactly this reason.

45_54.headline: You may be near the edge of the window — please talk to us soon.
45_54.body: For this kind of case, the window can extend into the mid to late 40s, but the exact limit depends on the specific offense, your specific age, and other details. Please reach out sooner rather than later so we can look at your case with you.

55_plus.headline: The general window may have passed for a criminal complaint, but other paths remain.
55_plus.body: For most sexual offenses committed against a minor by a family member or authority figure, the criminal window extends into the 40s — meaning the general limit may have passed. That said, there are exceptional cases where the law allows a later window, and a civil claim (which has different, often longer rules) may still be available to you. Please talk to us.
